q: Is Eq. 36 in the paper a typographical drop-out of a (g/δg)² factor, or is our algebra wrong?
basis: From the paper's own Eq. 35 (Var[σ_rw] = (Nwδg)² + Nw²(g² + δg²)) our derivation yields (δg/g)·sqrt(1 + 1/N + (g/δg)²/N), matched by MC to 3 digits at N=100, g=0.7, δg=0.07 (0.141 predicted, 0.141 MC). Eq. 36 as typeset in the pdftotext extraction reads two `1/N` terms with no (g/δg)² factor, giving 0.101 for the same numbers.
next_steps: Cross-check against the LaTeX source (arXiv preprint if available), sweep the two forms across (g, δg, N) to identify where they diverge maximally, and report a possible erratum to Palmer/Kronheim at UMD (or Phys. Rev. D).

q: How does the double-slit toy behave when g(x) is *learned* by a small DNN ensemble rather than known exactly?
basis: Sec. III.A uses exact analytic g(p) (Eq. 21) and Sec. V goes straight to a full HEP DNN. There is no controlled intermediate experiment isolating the systematic added by DNN-learning of g on a case where the true g is known.
next_steps: Fit a 20-net MLP ensemble to a 100k double-slit training set (binary pos-vs-neg classifier), compute learned g_hat(p) with PCA-based UQ, and quantify additional variance vs the exact-g baseline; report the ratio Var[σ_rw_learned] / Var[σ_rw_exact] as a function of network capacity.

q: For Sherpa-style samples with heterogeneous |w_n|, does the reweighted estimator require Σ |w_n| · g(x_n) or Σ w_signed_n · g(x_n)?
basis: Our double-slit replication demonstrated that the estimator that recovers ∫PDF is Σ|w|·g (from Eq. 6 identity). Signed w×g underestimates σ by ~30%. But paper's Eq. 27+ writes 'w_n · E[g(x_n)]' without disambiguating sign convention in Sherpa (where |w_n| varies event-by-event).
next_steps: Redo the derivation of Eq. 8 explicitly for Sherpa's weight-assignment (LHE-format signed w with |w|≠const); benchmark the two conventions on the actual ATLAS OpenData PhysLite V+jets samples and confirm which reproduces Fig. 5 nominal-vs-reweighted closure.

q: What is the sensitivity of the ~50% Asimov-significance improvement (2.56→3.84) to DNN ensemble size and loss function?
basis: Table VII reports the headline number for a 20-DNN ensemble with binary cross-entropy loss. Ensemble variance for PCA scaled as ~1/sqrt(N_ens); at N_ens=5 the PCA covariance estimate may be too noisy. Focal or class-weighted BCE may improve the rare-negative-weight modeling in cancellation regions.
next_steps: Sweep N_ens ∈ {5, 10, 20, 40, 80} at otherwise-fixed training config on ATLAS OpenData V+jets; report Asimov significance vs N_ens for both PCA and event-based UQ. Also try focal loss (gamma=2) and class-balanced BCE.

q: Does the reweighting introduce nonclosure at sparse high-multiplicity phase-space corners of the ZH signal region?
basis: Fig. 8 shows good pT(V) closure aggregated; the signal region (Table V) is heavily selected on nJets ∈ {2,3}, dijet-pT>150 GeV, btag>0.5. Eq. 38 crossover implies that per-bin the reweighting can *increase* total unc when N_bin is above threshold and δg is non-negligible — the exclusive tails may fail closure worse than the aggregate.
next_steps: Bin ATLAS OpenData V+jets in fine (pT(V), nJets, btag)-cells; compute per-cell nominal-vs-reweighted pull and per-cell (Var_rw - Var_nom)/Var_nom; identify cells where the reweighting hurts and correlate with local density.
